screening_decisions.reason: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot trial of intracervical nitroprusside gel immediately prior to IUD placement; measures patient-reported insertion pain (VAS). Meets population, intervention, comparator, and pain outcomes.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled ibuprofen 800 mg vs placebo 30–45 min before IUD insertion; primary outcome is pain at insertion (VAS). Eligible RCT on IUD insertion pain.
Randomised trial of full bladder vs immediate emptying at time of IUC insertion; compares provider ease and women’s pain scores. Nonpharmacologic pain-related approach with pain outcome. Eligible.

Randomized, open, parallel-group trial comparing 2% intracervical lidocaine injection vs ibuprofen 400 mg before LNG-IUS insertion; assesses pain at/after insertion. RCT with active comparator and relevant outcomes.
Double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of ibuprofen prophylaxis for LNG-IUS insertion; measures pain at tenaculum placement and insertion. Eligible RCT.
Double-blind, multicenter RCT of vaginal misoprostol 400 μg vs placebo 3 h before IUD insertion; includes pain and insertion-related outcomes. Eligible.
Randomized trial of buccal misoprostol 400 μg vs placebo 90 min prior to IUD insertion in nulliparous women; patient-reported pain at multiple time points (VAS). Eligible RCT.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study of sublingual misoprostol before repeat LNG-IUS insertion; reports ease and pain at insertion. Eligible.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of prophylactic ibuprofen 400 mg before copper IUD insertion; insertion pain measured by VAS. Eligible.
Single-blind randomized trial of sublingual misoprostol + diclofenac vs diclofenac alone before IUD insertion in women without prior vaginal delivery; includes pain and complications. Eligible RCT.
Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study of ibuprofen around IUD insertion; pain assessed during insertion and hours/days after. Eligible.
Randomized, double-blind clinical trial comparing oral tramadol, naproxen sodium, and placebo 1 h before IUD insertion; insertion pain (VAS) primary outcome. Eligible.
Double-blind RCT of buccal misoprostol vs placebo in nulliparous women; measures provider ease and patient-reported pain (VAS). Eligible.
Randomized, double-blind trial of intracervical 2% lidocaine gel vs placebo; pain measured at several time points including insertion. Eligible RCT.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot of vaginal nitroglycerin gel 30 min prior to LNG-IUS insertion; primary outcome: insertion pain. Eligible RCT.
Randomized trial of 1% lidocaine paracervical block vs no anesthetic before IUD insertion; patients rated pain at procedural steps including insertion. Eligible.
Block-randomized three-arm trial (lidocaine gel vs lubricant gel vs no intervention) with pain VAS immediately after copper IUD insertion; RCT with appropriate outcomes. Eligible.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot of intrauterine lidocaine infusion vs saline prior to IUD insertion; insertion pain measured. Eligible.
Randomized controlled trial of sublingual misoprostol + diclofenac vs diclofenac alone 1 h before copper IUD insertion in nulliparous women; assesses ease and pain. Eligible.
Randomized, double-blind clinical trial of vaginal misoprostol vs placebo 4 h prior to IUD insertion in nulligravidas; reports reduced moderate–severe pain; eligible RCT.

Randomized, placebo-controlled aromatherapy (lavender) vs placebo inhalation before IUD insertion; anxiety reduced and pain measured (no difference). Nonpharmacologic pain-related RCT with pain outcome. Eligible.
Randomized controlled trial of self-administered misoprostol vs placebo 3–4 h before IUD insertion in nulliparous women; measures insertion ease and pain. Eligible.

Randomized, placebo-controlled phase II trial of novel topical lidocaine formulation applied to cervix/uterus; significant pain reduction documented; pharmacokinetic phase I included. Eligible RCT for insertion pain.

Prospective, single-blinded, controlled three-arm study (paracervical lidocaine, placebo, no treatment) assessing pain during IUD insertion. Randomization not explicitly stated; at title/abstract stage, include due to uncertainty.
Registered randomized clinical trial of misoprostol vs placebo prior to IUD insertion in nulliparous women; primary outcome is insertion pain (VAS); provider ease also assessed. Eligible RCT.

Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of pre-insertion 2% lidocaine gel assessing VAS pain at tenaculum placement, during IUD insertion, and shortly after; directly matches RCT prevention criteria.
Experience/opinion piece describing intracervical block technique; no randomized controlled design or comparator arm.
Prospective cohort comparing parity groups; no randomized intervention to prevent insertion-related pain.
Qualitative study of perceptions among non-users; not an RCT of a pain-reduction intervention for IUD insertion.
Narrative/practical review without randomized trial data; not a primary RCT testing an analgesic intervention.
Methodological guidance on evidence grading; not specific to IUD insertion pain or an RCT.
Committee opinion on adolescent contraception; no randomized intervention aimed at reducing IUD insertion pain.
Review of strategies including RCTs, but not itself an RCT; does not provide primary randomized data for insertion pain.
Broad gynecologic review of misoprostol; not an RCT specifically evaluating IUD insertion pain outcomes.
Observational evaluation of expected vs actual pain with a specific insertion technique; no randomized analgesic comparison.
Evidence grading methodology article; not an RCT of an intervention for IUD insertion pain.
Nonrandomized study of predictors (ultrasound, history) for difficult/painful insertion; no interventional analgesic RCT.
Evidence overview/recommendations; not a primary randomized controlled trial.
Systematic review across procedures; not a primary RCT on IUD insertion pain (and reports insufficient evidence for IUD insertion).
Observational questionnaire-based assessment of premedication use and anxiety; no randomization/comparator trial.
Technical report on adolescent contraception; not an RCT of insertion pain reduction.
Meta-analysis of RCTs; secondary research, not a primary randomized controlled trial within this batch.
RCT in a different procedure (cervical ripening before first-trimester surgical termination); does not evaluate IUD insertion pain.
Survey of practitioners’ techniques and policies; no randomized interventional evaluation for insertion pain.
Methodology/protocol for PMA on misoprostol and IUD insertion ease; not reporting an RCT on pain outcomes.
Commentary/review arguing against misoprostol; not a randomized controlled trial.
Randomized, double-blind trial treating post-insertion cramps over subsequent days; not a prophylactic intervention targeting insertion pain (tenaculum/insertion/up to 6h) as prevention.

Randomized clinical trial with lavender aromatherapy vs placebo (sesame oil) vs control before IUD insertion; VAS pain during/after insertion assessed; aligns with RCT prevention of insertion-related pain.
Descriptive technique report without randomized allocation or controlled comparison.
Cochrane review summarizing RCTs (including prophylactic use) but not a primary randomized trial from this batch.
